advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that injects a model_override whose object profile would select NativeOutput (e.g. a FunctionModel with supports_json_schema_output=True or a config string that disagrees) and asserts the run still takes the PromptedOutput path, so the model_override arm of `caps = capabilities_for(resolved if ...)` is guarded against reading the double's profile.
evidence: runner.py:353: `caps = capabilities_for(resolved if self._model_override is not None else model)`
Diff rationale: 'an override run must keep resolving from the config string, since a test double's own profile would otherwise select NativeOutput and exhaust the bounded output retry.'

All model_override structured tests use a default-profile FunctionModel with `_cfg()`/`LLMConfig(repo_path='.')` (claude default) — e.g. test_pydantic_ai_runner.py:122-138 test_structured_mode_returns_validated_payload, test_runner_structured_schema.py:72-80. A base ModelProfile has supports_json_schema_output=False (capabilities.py:74 reads `getattr(profile,'supports_json_schema_output',False)`), so both `model` (FunctionModel) and `resolved` (anthropic:...) yield native_structured_output=False -> PromptedOutput.

ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit injects a model_override whose `.profile` would select NativeOutput while the resolved config string selects PromptedOutput (or vice versa), so a regression flipping the ternary would pass every existing test.
advisory.finding: The new model_override arm of the caps resolution in run() — `capabilities_for(resolved if self._model_override is not None else model)` — is not covered by any test that would fail if it regressed to reading `model`. Every existing model_override test uses a bare FunctionModel whose base ModelProfile.supports_json_schema_output defaults to False, so both the string path (`resolved`) and the object path (`model`) resolve to PromptedOutput identically; the branch's discriminating behavior is invisible to them. The diff's own rationale frames reading the double's profile as a real hazard ('a test double's own profile would otherwise select NativeOutput and exhaust the bounded output retry'), yet no test constructs a model_override whose object profile disagrees with the config string.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test in test_pydantic_ai_runner.py that builds a FunctionModel whose `.profile` reports supports_json_schema_output=True (or monkeypatches its profile), runs a structured request via model_override with a claude/default config, and asserts the structured output is produced through PromptedOutput (not NativeOutput) — i.e. it succeeds where a NativeOutput selection would exhaust the retry. This fails if the ternary is inverted to read `model`.
